Hi Veronica, Avery —

Thanks for the attachments. Confirming Redwood's execution plan and the details you asked for below. Please see inline answers and the signatory matrix at the end.

Execution plan (DocuSign):
- Envelope template: "DPA_Master_RI_2026" (will be created from redwood-esign-template-RI-2026.stamp).
- Signing order: Redwood executes first. We set Marissa Cole as the initial signer (Head of Legal Ops). Once signed, envelope routes to Integra signers.
- Countersign options: DocuSign supports both sequential and parallel signing. For parallel countersign we will set Integra signers as parallel recipients after Redwood completes. Note: parallel countersign means both Integra and Redwood entries are time-stamped; however, some customers' internal policy still requires GC review prior to clicking sign.
- Authentication: default is email-based authentication. If Integra requires ID verify or phone OTP, we can enable DocuSign ID Verification or SMS OTP (will require signer's phone number and a one-time fee).
- Audit & retention: signed PDF plus DocuSign audit trail will be retained in Redwood's contract repository. We can provide a signed copy and the full audit trail PDF on request.

Signatory matrix (to attach to PO):
- Redwood Inference
  - Marissa Cole — Head of Legal Ops — marissa_cole@redwood.com
  - Christopher Yang — CFO — chris_yang@redwood.com (backup signer for high-value deals)

- IntegraHealth
  - Veronica Lin — Contracts Manager — v.lin@integrahealth.com
  - Procurement Team — procurement@integrahealth.com

Notes: If Integra's GC requires countersign prior to signature, we can reconfigure to route to them for review and require their signed consent before sending to your procurement runner. That will add ~1 business day.
